## Description

**What**: Create the bug-classifier-haiku agent and wire mandatory dispatch into /dso:fix-bug at the closure phase.
**Why**: SC3 requires every Fixed: closure to carry a bug-type-<slug> tag. The classifier agent and the dispatch hook are the operational core of the registry — without them the registry is reference-only.
**Scope**:
- IN: plugins/dso/agents/bug-classifier-haiku.md; modifications to /dso:fix-bug SKILL.md to add mandatory dispatch AFTER GREEN verification and BEFORE ticket transition (not in the existing Anti-Pattern Sweep / Test Index Phase G — name the new step explicitly); byte-exact output validation; failure-marker fallback
- OUT: Other skills that close bugs (handled by S6); backfill (S3); retro (S4)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/agents/bug-classifier-haiku.md exists defining the bug-classifier-haiku agent with prompt: classify using registry slug list (from S1's machine-readable export), return a single registry slug or 'uncategorized'; partial match is not a match; return 'uncategorized' if no slug would be answered yes without caveats
  <- Satisfies: "SC3: Dispatch input: registry slug list with classification questions, bug title and description, fix diff summary"
- When this story is complete, /dso:fix-bug SKILL.md contains a new, explicitly-named bug-type classification step positioned AFTER the GREEN verification phase and BEFORE the closing ticket transition command; the existing Anti-Pattern Sweep & Test Index Phase G content is unchanged; the new step's position and ordering relative to Phase G and Phase H Step 1 is stated explicitly
  <- Satisfies: "SC3: /dso:fix-bug Phase G — MANDATORY bug classifier dispatch" (adversarial finding: phase name disambiguation)
- When this story is complete, the orchestrator dispatches bug-classifier-haiku on every closure with --reason="Fixed:..." and skips ONLY on --reason="Escalated to user:..." (keyed to reason prefix)
  <- Satisfies: "SC3: MANDATORY on Fixed: closure; Skip: Escalated to user: prefix"
- When this story is complete, output validation: orchestrator trims whitespace then byte-for-byte compares against registry_slugs union {uncategorized}; ANY deviation is schema failure; valid output writes bug-type-<slug> via ticket tag CLI
  <- Satisfies: "SC3: Output validation: byte-for-exactly compares"
- When this story is complete, schema/timeout/dispatch-error failure writes BOTH bug-type-uncategorized AND bug-type-classifier-failed-<reason> where <reason> is one of: timeout, schema, dispatch-error (dash-delimited, no colons); failed tag-write retried once; on second failure a comment is posted recording the failure
  <- Satisfies: "SC3: Failure writes both tags; retry once; comment on second failure"
- When this story is complete, the classifier dispatch is explicitly exempted from MAX_AGENTS/SESSION_USAGE throttle gating — it is a single short haiku call that must run even when MAX_AGENTS=0 to prevent permanently mis-classified tickets; the exemption is documented in the SKILL.md step
  <- Satisfies: reliability consideration (adversarial finding)
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Integration] The Jira inbound bridge (_handle_edit.py) overwrites local tags with Jira labels on each inbound sync. After this story writes a bug-type-<slug> tag locally, the next inbound sync can strip it if Jira does not echo it back. Implementation-plan must choose: (a) add bug-type-* to a no-overwrite allowlist in _handle_edit.py, (b) push bug-type-* outbound to Jira, or (c) document jira-* tickets as exempt from SC3 and adjust stats expectations in S4.
- [Reliability] Document explicitly whether the classifier dispatch is exempted from MAX_AGENTS throttling (recommendation: yes — exempt it; see Done Definition above).

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I can see each closed bug automatically tagged with its bug-type slug so that classification happens systematically at fix time
